answers.answer: 1. Four players use 3 randomly chosen Escape Pods. 2. Place the lowest-numbered in Section A, next number in B, then alternate A/B; all start Locked side up. 3. Put 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults plus 1 additional Adult per player (7 Adults total) in the bag.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 7 and 10; Key numbers

answers.answer: 1. Remove cards from both Personal and Corporate decks showing a player count higher than the actual count, shuffle decks separately, and deal each player one of each face down. 2. Deal these before Character draft. 3. At the first Encounter—when the first Intruder miniature appears—each player chooses one of their two Objectives and removes the other face down from the game without looking at others' removed cards; resolve the triggering Encounter afterward. 4. Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this choice.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 16–17; Critical gameplay moments—First Encounter

requested_parts: payment for printed cost 2 Action card
answers.answer: 1. Discard the Action card being played face up, plus exactly 2 additional Action cards to pay its printed cost. 2. Contamination cards cannot pay any Action cost. 3. If the card has sections separated by OR, choose one section.
answers.evidence: Actions—Action Cost; Actions from Action cards

answers.answer: 1. A Character ending their own round in a burning Room takes 1 Light Wound, after finishing that round. A player who passes takes this once at the end of that round. 2. Once passed, they cannot take further normal Actions that Player Phase (FAQ permits Interruption after passing). 3. When passing, they may discard any number of cards from hand. 4. Later players' rounds do not burn them again that turn; Fire damage is checked at the end of their own round only.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure—Player rounds; FAQ & Rulings—Rounds, events, damage and Intruders

answers.answer: 1. On entry to an unexplored Room, flip the tile face up and reveal and resolve its Exploration token; special Rooms count as already explored. 2. Rotate the tile so the token's item number faces the printed Item Counter; do not set a counter in the Nest or Room Covered With Slime. 3. Resolve its effect, then remove the token from game to the box. 4. If the Room is empty, roll Noise; results 1–4 place Noise in the connected Corridor with that number (include Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance). If a marker is already there, resolve an Encounter. 5. Exploration Silence normally suppresses that movement's Noise roll; with Slime, resolve Danger instead. 6. Exploration Danger suppresses the roll and moves all eligible neighboring Intruders not in Combat into the Room; if none are eligible, place Noise in every connected Corridor lacking a marker. 7. If any Character or Intruder is already in the entered Room, do not roll Noise. (Careful Movement and Reconnaissance also replace/cancel automatic Silence/Danger results.)
answers.evidence: Movement, Rooms, and Corridors; Exploration tokens; Noise roll; Careful Movement

answers.answer: 1. Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards. 2. It follows normal movement restrictions and replaces the post-move Noise roll with placing a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the destination; it also replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration results (Reconnaissance cancels those automatic results too). 3. It cannot be used while in Combat, and is forbidden if all Corridors connected to the destination already contain Noise. 4. A Closed Door blocks Character movement across its Corridor. 5. Characters and Intruders may occupy only Rooms; nobody may stop in a Corridor.
answers.evidence: Basic Actions—Careful Movement; Movement, Rooms, and Corridors

answers.answer: 1. On a Noise result directing placement where Noise already exists, resolve an Encounter: discard all Noise in all Corridors connected to the Room, including Technical Corridors if connected; draw one Intruder token and place its matching miniature in the Encounter Room. 2. Thus connected existing Noise is cleared before the draw. 3. A result for a Technical Corridor Entrance places Noise on the shared Technical Corridors space, treated as every such Entrance; when an Intruder moves there it disappears, loses Injury markers and its token returns to the bag (Noise there remains). The drawn non-Blank Encounter token is set aside outside the bag until a rule returns it. 4. Fewer hand cards than token number causes a Surprise Attack on the triggering Character; equal or more means none. A Blank restores connected Noise and returns to bag instead of placing a miniature; if it was last in bag, add an available Adult. 5. Contamination cards count as hand cards for the comparison.
answers.evidence: Technical Corridors; Encounters; Combat quick reference

requested_parts: movement into Character Room as Encounter
answers.answer: 1. Move all eligible neighboring Intruders (those not in Combat with any Character) into the Room. 2. If none are eligible, put a Noise marker in every connected Corridor that lacks one, including Technical Corridors if there is an Entrance. 3. An Intruder merely moving into a Room with a Character is not an Encounter; they are simply in Combat. 4. A Character with Slime resolves a Silence result as Danger.
answers.evidence: Exploration tokens—Danger; Noise roll; Encounters; Slime marker

answers.answer: 1. During an Encounter, Blank places Noise in each Corridor connected to that Room; the Encounter ends without a miniature. 2. Return Blank to the bag. 3. If it was the last token in the bag, add an Adult token if one is available, otherwise nothing. 4. During bag development, Blank adds one Adult to the bag if available, then Blank returns to the bag; it does not cause the Encounter procedure or restore Noise.
answers.evidence: Encounters—Blank token in an Encounter; Intruder bag development—Blank

requested_parts: two Intruders through one Closed Door
answers.answer: 1. Intruders attempting to move together from a Room through one Closed Door all stay in their starting Room. 2. They destroy the Door simultaneously. 3. A Destroyed Door is represented by a lying token, permits movement and cannot be Closed again (except Plasma Torch). 4. An Intruder appearing due to a Noise roll comes through a Closed Door regardless of it.
answers.evidence: Fire, Malfunction, Doors, Slime and Noise markers—Door tokens; FAQ Rules 8

answers.answer: 1. When the Intruder moves to a Technical Corridors Entrance, it disappears into the ducts. 2. Remove its miniature and all its Injury markers. 3. Return its token to the bag; do not remove any Noise marker on the Technical Corridors space. 4. Characters cannot use Technical Corridors except through the Mechanic's Technical Corridors Action card or Technical Corridor Plans Item. 5. Door tokens can never be placed in Technical Corridors.
answers.evidence: Technical Corridors

answers.answer: 1. Shoot costs 1 Action card and 1 Ammo. Choose a Weapon in hand and one Intruder in your Room, discard 1 Ammo, roll Combat die; on injury apply markers and check Injury Effect. 2. Melee costs 1 Action card; draw a Contamination card onto your Action discard pile, choose an Intruder in your Room and roll. 3. Both target Intruders in your Room. 4. Melee adds one Contamination card. 5. A Shoot miss has no Wound penalty; a Melee miss causes 1 Serious Wound. 6. A double-hit result deals 2 Injuries in Shoot and 1 Injury in Melee.
answers.evidence: Combat quick reference; Combat—Shoot and Melee table

answers.answer: 1. Larva dies at 1 Injury; no Carcass. 2. Adult draws one Intruder Attack card and dies if blood value is less than or equal to its current total Injuries. 3. Queen draws two Attack cards and dies if their blood values summed are less than or equal to its current injuries. 4. On death, Adult and Queen miniatures are removed and a Carcass is placed in the Room. 5. If either of the Queen's two drawn cards shows a Retreat arrow, retreat resolves instead of the numerical death check: draw an Event card and move the Queen through the Corridor number shown in its Intruder movement section, then discard that Event card.
answers.evidence: Combat—Intruder Injuries and death; Intruder Retreat

answers.answer: 1. Before moving, resolve one Intruder Attack per Intruder in the Room, starting with larger types: Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva. 2. Escape attacks target the escaping Character; Larva Infests rather than drawing an Attack card. 3. If the Character dies, their Corpse stays in the Room they attempted to leave. 4. If they survive, complete movement to the chosen neighboring Room and resolve exploration and Noise as usual (Noise only if destination is empty).
answers.evidence: Character Escape; Intruder Attack

answers.answer: 1. With several Characters in the Room, target the Character whose player has the fewest Action cards in hand. 2. On a tie, target the First Player token holder or next player in turn order. (A Surprise Attack targets its trigger; an Escape attack targets the escaper.) 3. For non-Larva, draw one Intruder Attack card; matching attacking Intruder symbol means resolve effect, otherwise miss; ignore blood icon. 4. Larva draws no Attack card: remove its miniature and put it on target's Character board. If the target already has a Larva, attacking Larva disappears and existing Larva stays; target still gains Contamination and is not automatically killed. 5. Put gained Contamination on top of target's Action discard pile.
answers.evidence: Intruder Attack; Infest; Contamination cards and Infection

answers.answer: 1. No. Dressing flips a Serious Wound face down so its effect is ignored, but it still counts toward the three-wound limit; with 3 Serious Wounds, any further Wound kills. 2. A third Light Wound clears the Light Wound track and becomes a Serious Wound. 3. Heal removes a Light Wound or discards a Dressed Serious Wound, as specified by the healing effect. 4. On death, place the Character Corpse token in the Room as an Object. 5. Drop all Heavy Objects in that Room; Items disappear from the game.
answers.evidence: Character Wounds and death; FAQ Rulings—death

answers.answer: 1. Canteen and Shower scan all Contamination cards in the Character's HAND only; remove scanned non-Infected cards from game. An Infected card stays; with no Larva, place one Larva, and if one already exists the Character dies and a Creeper appears in the Room. Shower also removes Slime. 2. Surgery scans all Contamination cards in deck, hand and discard; removes all Infected cards and removes a Larva from the board if present. 3. Surgery costs the normal Room Action cost of 2 Action cards, causes 1 Light Wound, then the player automatically passes and shuffles all cards—including the whole hand and remaining Contamination—into the Action deck; hand remains empty until next turn. It does not give a new Contamination card.
answers.evidence: Contamination scan table; Room Actions—Canteen, Shower, Surgery; FAQ Items 9

answers.answer: 1. In a Room with uncarried Eggs, Shoot or Melee may target Eggs; each Injury destroys one Egg. 2. Grenade thrown at a Room with uncarried Eggs destroys 2; Molotov destroys 1. 3. Fire destroys 1 uncarried Egg in that Room each Fire Damage step. 4. A missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor Wound; whether successful Egg Melee incurs Contamination is unresolved in the summary. 5. After every single attempt to destroy an Egg, roll Noise. Throwing Grenade/Molotov from another Room rolls Noise in your own Room. 6. When no Eggs remain on the Intruder board, the Nest is destroyed and marked with an Injury marker.
answers.evidence: Eggs and the Nest; source limitations—Contamination on successful Egg Melee unresolved

answers.answer: 1. Enter via the corresponding Evacuation Section Room Action, costing 2 cards; Pod must be unlocked with a free space, and Section must have neither Intruder nor Malfunction. 2. Roll Noise first; if an Intruder appears or reaches the Section, entry fails. 3. Each Pod holds 2 Characters. 4. Heavy Objects do not take a Character space. 5. After boarding, either launch immediately or wait and pass the current turn. On later Player Phases, at the start of your first round choose exactly one: keep waiting and pass, launch, or exit free to Section Room and take a full 2-Action round. 6. While waiting you count as present in the Section for bag-development Noise rolls; a second Character can launch the Pod immediately with both aboard; an Intruder appearing there sends all Pod occupants back to the Room. Malfunction blocks new entry only; waiting, launch or exit remain allowed.
answers.evidence: Escape Pods

answers.answer: 1. Victory checks proceed Engines, Coordinates, Contamination, Objectives. 2. If ship survives to Engine check, reveal all three top tokens; 2 or 3 Damaged Engines destroy the ship and kill everything aboard, including sleepers and Intruders. 3. If it survives, reveal Coordinates; non-Earth destination kills hibernating Characters while ship remains intact and Intruders live. 4. A sleeper with Quarantine Objective survives if destination is Mars. 5. At Contamination check, every surviving Character: with no Larva, scan all Contamination in Action deck, hand and discard. If none Infected, no four-card draw. If any Infected or a Larva is present, shuffle all Action and Contamination cards from deck, hand and discard together and draw top 4; any Contamination among four kills, regardless of Infected status. This procedure does not remove cards merely for scanning non-Infected. 6. Launched Pod passengers also take the final Contamination and Objective checks.
answers.evidence: Victory Check; Key numbers

answers.answer: 1. Shuffle Room tiles 2 unseen and place one face down on each 2 slot; return extras unseen. Repeat for all Room 1 tiles on 1 slots. 2. Shuffle Exploration tokens unseen, put one face down on each Room, return extras. 3. Put one random Coordinates card face down by Cockpit. 4. Put Destination marker on B space of Destination Track. 5. Put Time marker on green Time Track space. 6. For each of 3 Engines, shuffle one Working and one Damaged token face down and stack on matching Engine slot; top is true status. 7. Put 5 Eggs on Intruder board. 8. Place 3 random Weakness cards face down in Intruder board slots.
answers.evidence: Setup—Board setup steps 2–13; Key numbers

answers.answer: 1. Deal each player a numbered Help card (1 through player count); that and matching Inventory number set Player Number and draft order. 2. Shuffle draft cards. Player 1 draws 2 and reveals both publicly, keeps one, shuffles other back; repeat in player-number order. 3. Each gets Character board and miniature with colored ring in Hibernatorium, shuffled 10-card Action deck, Starting Weapon in a Hand slot loaded to its Ammo capacity, and two Quest Items horizontal/inactive beside board. 4. Blue Character Corpse starts in Hibernatorium. 5. Quest Items are not active at start; unlock via their mini-quest conditions.
answers.evidence: Crew setup steps 14–20

answers.answer: 1. At start of each Player Phase, every player draws to 5 cards (6 if Cabins passive applies). 2. After drawing, pass First Player token left except on first game turn. 3. If Action deck empties when a draw is needed, shuffle discard pile into a new deck and continue. 4. Used Actions and gained Contamination go on that Character's Action discard pile; Item discards to matching Item discard, Events to Event discard, Intruder Attack to its discard, Serious Wounds to their discard, markers to marker pool. Search/Storage's rejected Item goes face down to bottom of chosen deck. 5. Normal discards are face up; card-holder normal Item cards are hidden, with only backs/colors visible; Heavy Items/Objects are visible.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure; Discard piles; Items and Objects

answers.answer: 1. Advance Time (and active Self-Destruct), Intruders in Combat attack, Intruders in Fire take Injury and resolve Injury Effect, resolve Event movement then its effect, then bag development. 2. On Event card, all Intruders showing its symbol that are not in a Room with Characters move. 3. Each moves to neighboring Room through Corridor matching card number; if it indicates Technical Corridor, remove miniature and return token to bag. 4. Resolve event effect after movement. 5. When Event deck runs out, shuffle Event discards into new deck. 6. When Intruder Attack deck runs out, shuffle its discard pile into new deck.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure—Event Phase; Intruder Attack; FAQ Rulings

answers.answer: 1. Draw Larva: remove that token from bag and add Adult token to bag. 2. Draw Creeper: remove it and add Breeder token. 3. Draw Adult: return it immediately before all players roll Noise in order, skipping Characters in Combat; those Encounters may draw that same Adult. 4. Draw Breeder: players roll Noise in order, skipping Combat, then return Breeder. 5. Draw Queen: if any Character is in Nest, place Queen and resolve Encounter; otherwise add Egg to Intruder board. Return Queen token. 6. Draw Blank: add available Adult, then return Blank. 7. The turn ends only after bag development and any resulting Encounters/Surprise Attacks are fully resolved; then next turn begins.
answers.evidence: Intruder bag development; Turn Structure—End of the turn

answers.answer: 1. If told to place a Fire marker when all 8 are in use, ship explodes and game ends. 2. Same for all 8 Malfunction markers: hull integrity lost and game ends. 3. Max one of either per Room; extra placements in a Room already marked do nothing. 4. Removed Fire markers return to pool; removed Malfunction markers return to pool. 5. Hull loss kills all Characters aboard, awake and hibernated, and everything else aboard including Intruders; launched Pod passengers are away and remain eligible for Victory Check.
answers.evidence: Fire, Malfunction, Doors, Slime and Noise markers; End of the game

answers.answer: 1. Malfunction makes the Room's Action unavailable and makes its Computer unavailable. 2. Searching remains allowed; repair effects can remove Malfunction. 3. Cannot be placed in Nest, Room Covered With Slime, or an unexplored Room. 4. Does not change Engine token status; it only disables Engine Room action. 5. A Malfunction in Hibernatorium does not affect already-hibernated Characters.
answers.evidence: Fire, Malfunction, Doors, Slime and Noise markers

answers.answer: 1. Normal Item cards in Inventory are hidden. 2. Other players see only backs/colors. 3. There is no normal Item Inventory size limit. 4. Any Item used must be shown to all players. 5. Heavy Items and Objects must be visible and occupy one of 2 Hand slots; maximum 2 carried. Heavy Objects include Eggs, Character Corpses and Intruder Carcasses. 6. Add-type Items attach to another card and act as one. 7. Duct Tape combines 2 Heavy Items into one Hand slot, never Objects.
answers.evidence: Items and Objects—Inventory; Heavy Items and Objects

answers.answer: 1. A dropped Item is lost and discarded. 2. A dropped Object stays in the Room. 3. Dropping is free, at any time during your turn, with no Action. 4. Weapons found by Searching start with 1 Ammo. 5. Starting Weapon is loaded with Ammo markers equal to printed capacity; Weapons never exceed capacity.
answers.evidence: Items and Objects—Drop; Crew setup step 18

answers.answer: 1. Search chooses among Red, Yellow or Green deck matching Room color; in white Room choose any of these three. 2. Draw 2 from chosen deck and keep 1. 3. Put rejected card face down on bottom of that deck. 4. Each Search lowers Room Item Counter by 1. 5. At zero it cannot be searched, except Scout's Scavenging. 6. Nest and Room Covered With Slime prohibit Search; Storage Room Action is separate and works even at zero. 7. Blue Crafted Items are never found by Searching.
answers.evidence: Items and Objects—Searching; FAQ Rooms 6

answers.answer: 1. Craft Item is a Basic Action costing 1 Action card and discarding 2 Item cards. 2. Their blue Component icons must match the two gray icons on result card. 3. Result cannot be built if its card is unavailable, even with components. 4. Craft deck may be inspected at any time. 5. Items and component pairs: Antidote—flame + medical cross; Taser—battery/lightning + screwdriver/tool; Flamethrower—flame + screwdriver/tool; Molotov Cocktail—flame + folded cloth/fabric.
answers.evidence: Basic Actions—Craft Item; Crafting

answers.answer: 1. Only the player initiating Trade pays one Action card. 2. All Characters in the Room can trade with each other, including non-initiators; parties must agree. 3. You may give Item/Object for nothing. 4. Characters cannot exchange Ammo. 5. Heavy Items found by Searching do not require a separate Pick Up Heavy Object Action; that action applies to Objects only.
answers.evidence: Basic Actions—Trade and Pick Up Heavy Object; FAQ Actions 1–2

answers.answer: 1. Laboratory can Analyse a Character Corpse, Intruder Carcass or Egg, revealing corresponding Weakness card. 2. That Object must be present in Laboratory when analysed; Scientist's location does not substitute. 3. Object is retained, not consumed. 4. Revealed Weakness rule benefits all players. 5. Discover Weakness Objective is satisfied when anyone researched a corresponding Object in Laboratory before end; you need not personally research it.
answers.evidence: Room Actions—Laboratory; FAQ Rooms 3–4; Objective types

requested_parts: Room Action common prerequisites and cost
Fire effects on Room Actions and Searching
answers.answer: 1. Room Action normally costs 2 Action cards; Character must be in Room, not in Combat, and Room must not have Malfunction. 2. A Computer icon itself has no separate stated effect here; it identifies Computer access and a Malfunction makes Room's Computer unavailable. 3. Fire does not prevent Room Actions or Searching; a Character ending their round in Fire takes a Light Wound.
answers.evidence: Room Actions; Fire, Malfunction, Doors, Slime and Noise markers

answers.answer: 1. Armory adds Ammo to one of your Energy Weapons. 2. Add 2 Ammo. 3. Cannot recharge Classic Weapons or exceed Weapon's printed Ammo capacity.
answers.evidence: Player Reference—Room Actions, Armory

answers.answer: 1. Choose one: Dress all your Serious Wounds; Heal one Dressed Serious Wound; or Heal all your Light Wounds. 2. Dressing flips card face down so its effect is ignored; wound still counts and is not removed. 3. Duplicate Serious Wound card effects are not cumulative.
answers.evidence: Player Reference—Emergency Room; Character Wounds and death

answers.answer: 1. Send a Signal places a Status marker on your Character board's Signal space. 2. It is used only for Objectives. 3. Comms Room is always aboard in the basic game.
answers.evidence: Player Reference—Comms Room; Objective types

answers.answer: 1. Choose any one Room. 2. Discard its Fire marker if it has one. 3. All Intruders there run away in random directions, drawing one Event card per Intruder. 4. It also works when Room has no Fire, to scatter Intruders.
answers.evidence: Player Reference—Fire Control System

answers.answer: 1. Generator Room Action starts by placing marker on first green Self-Destruct space. 2. Any Character may stop by removing marker; restarting begins again at green. 3. Advance marker one space whenever Time marker advances. 4. At first yellow, cannot abort and all Pods unlock; they may be re-Locked and later yellow spaces do not unlock again. 5. Final skull space explodes ship. 6. If hyperspace jump occurs while Self-Destruct active, ship is still considered destroyed. 7. Character cannot start it while anyone is hibernating; Coolant Leak Event can start it despite sleepers.
answers.evidence: Self-Destruct sequence; FAQ Rules 14, 25

answers.answer: 1. Choose any one OTHER Yellow Room. 2. Its connected Corridors must contain no Destroyed Door. 3. Immediately Close every Door around it and put Airlock Procedure token there. 4. At end of current Player Phase (all players passed), if every Door remains Closed, everything in the Room dies and Fire marker is removed. If any Door is opened first, cancel procedure.
answers.evidence: Player Reference—Airlock Control

answers.answer: 1. At start of a new turn, a Character in Cabins with no Intruder present draws one extra Action card. 2. Hand is 6 rather than 5. 3. Malfunction disables this passive. 4. It is passive, not a paid Room Action.
answers.evidence: Player Reference—Cabins; Key numbers

answers.answer: 1. Command Center can choose any one Room, including a distant Room. 2. Open or Close any chosen Doors in its connected Corridors; player chooses which. 3. Destroyed Door cannot be Closed again, so not a valid close target.
answers.evidence: Player Reference—Command Center; Door tokens

answers.answer: 1. Engine Control Room checks status of all three Engines. 2. It cannot change Engine status. 3. Check works even if an Engine Room has a Malfunction marker; Malfunction only disables that Room's own Action and does not change Engine token.
answers.evidence: Player Reference—Engine Control Room; Engines

answers.answer: 1. Hatch Control flips one Escape Pod token to Locked or Unlocked. 2. Monitoring Room secretly looks at any one unexplored Room tile and its Exploration token. 3. It is for unexplored location. 4. Look at both tile and token. 5. You may lie about what you saw. 6. Replace them after inspection.
answers.evidence: Player Reference—Hatch Control System; Monitoring Room

answers.answer: 1. Entering Room Covered With Slime automatically gives Slime; no Action needed. 2. No Item count is set. 3. Malfunction cannot be placed there. 4. Maximum one Slime marker; additional Slime does nothing. 5. Shower removes Slime but does not extinguish Fire; Fire may exist there normally.
answers.evidence: Exploration tokens—Slime; Player Reference—Room Covered With Slime and Shower

answers.answer: 1. Check Coordinates by secretly looking at Coordinates card, or Set Destination by moving Destination marker. 2. Coordinates may be kept secret; you may lie about what you saw. 3. Destination marker selects one of four entries on Coordinates card corresponding to track space; this determines ship's jump destination. 4. You cannot change Destination once anyone is hibernating. 5. You cannot Set Destination with an Intruder in Cockpit.
answers.evidence: Player Reference—Cockpit

answers.answer: 1. Check secretly looks at top Engine token. Repair/Break secretly examine both tokens and restack them in any order. 2. You may lie about check and need not say whether you repaired it. 3. You must announce if you changed the token order. 4. No prior check is required. 5. Repair/Break works despite a Malfunction in Engine Room.
answers.evidence: Player Reference—Engines #1–#3

answers.answer: 1. Hibernation only when Time is on a blue space; pay 2 cards while in Hibernatorium, with no Intruder or Malfunction there. 2. Roll Noise; an Intruder reaching or appearing in Room makes attempt fail. 3. Otherwise remove miniature; Character stops participating until end checks. 4. Once anyone hibernates, no Character may change Destination or initiate Self-Destruct. Coolant Leak Event can still initiate Self-Destruct. 5. Later Hibernatorium Malfunction does not wake or harm sleepers.
answers.evidence: Player Reference—Hibernatorium; Hibernation opens; FAQ Rules 13–14

answers.answer: 1. When Time reaches final red space, ship jumps immediately; awake Characters aboard die from g-force, Intruders are unharmed. 2. Game also ends when last alive non-hibernating Character aboard dies, hibernates or launches. If no Self-Destruct active, move Time to final red; if active, move it to final skull and resolve. 3. Active Self-Destruct thus explodes ship in this end condition. 4. Intruders do not die from an ordinary hyperspace jump.
answers.evidence: End of the game

answers.answer: 1. Characters cannot directly attack other Characters because of anti-aggression implants. 2. Actions can harm crew indirectly, for example locking someone in a burning Room, activating Self-Destruct with people aboard, or throwing a Grenade into a Room with other crew.
answers.evidence: Attacking other players

requested_parts: all models in Combat unresolved case
answers.answer: 1. If an Adult must appear and all 8 models are on board, remove all Adult models not in Combat and return their tokens to bag if possible; then place an Adult in Encounter Room. 2. If all 8 Adults are in Combat, summary says the source does not explain how to supply a model; authoritative clarification needed. 3. An Intruder ending movement in an unexplored Room remains there; do not remove it, reveal tile or Exploration token.
answers.evidence: Encounters—Adult overflow; Intruders in unexplored Rooms; Source limitations

answers.answer: 1. Small curled symbol in Shoot hits Larva or Creeper for 1 Injury; it misses all other types. 2. Larger curved symbol in Shoot hits Larva, Creeper or Adult for 1 Injury; misses Breeder or Queen. 3. In Melee, small symbol has same target restriction and 1 Injury; ineligible target is a miss and causes attacker 1 Serious Wound. 4. Larger symbol same: eligible target takes 1 Injury; ineligible target means miss and 1 Serious Wound.
answers.evidence: Combat die result table

requested_parts: final check with no Larva and all scans non-Infected
answers.answer: 1. If no Larva and every Contamination card scanned from deck, hand and discard is non-Infected, the Character does not draw four cards. 2. The cards are not removed merely because they scan non-Infected; endgame procedure does not remove them. 3. A launched Pod passenger still faces final Contamination and Objective checks, so earlier launch does not bypass Objective check.
answers.evidence: Victory Check—Contamination and Objectives; Escape Pods—Launch immediately

answers.answer: 1. Antidote: flame + medical cross. 2. Taser: battery/lightning + screwdriver/tool. 3. Flamethrower: flame + screwdriver/tool. 4. Molotov Cocktail: flame + folded cloth/fabric. These refer to blue Component symbols on discarded Items matching gray icons on Crafted card.
answers.evidence: Crafting—four Crafted Items and component symbols

answers.answer: 1. You are in Combat whenever an Intruder is in your Room; Eggs are not Intruders. 2. In Combat Only restrictions permit use only while Intruder shares Room. 3. Out of Combat Only restrictions permit use only without Intruder in Room. 4. Unmarked card and Item Actions work in or out of Combat subject to requirements; Basic Actions in Combat are limited to Shoot, Melee and Basic Movement as Escape, and Room Actions are forbidden. 5. Eggs do not cause Combat.
answers.evidence: Actions—In Combat / Out of Combat

answers.answer: 1. For Player X's Character cannot survive, that Character must be dead at game end. 2. You do not have to kill them with your own Actions. 3. Hibernating or escaping means they survive, so does not satisfy cannot-survive. 4. Only survivor means no other Character may survive. 5. Regardless, your own Character must survive by Escape Pod or hibernation and fulfill your Objective.
answers.evidence: Objective types; Winning

answers.answer: 1. If a Door must be placed and pool is empty, move any Door token from elsewhere on board. 2. Open is no token. 3. Closed is standing token. 4. Destroyed is lying token; cannot be Closed again except Plasma Torch. 5. Maximum one Door token per Corridor. 6. Doors can never be placed in Technical Corridors.
answers.evidence: Door tokens; Technical Corridors

requested_parts: first Character death while Pods Locked
answers.answer: 1. First dead Character automatically unlocks all Escape Pods immediately. 2. Flip all Pods to Unlocked. 3. They may subsequently be Locked or Unlocked normally, for example by Hatch Control System.
answers.evidence: Critical gameplay moments—First dead Character; Escape Pods

requested_parts: Storage Room Action draw and keep
common Room Action cost and restrictions
answers.answer: 1. Storage Room Action draws 2 cards from a chosen Red, Yellow or Green Item deck and keeps 1. It works repeatedly even at Item Counter zero. 2. Put rejected card face down at bottom of chosen deck. 3. Normal Room Action costs 2 Action cards; must be in Room, cannot be used in Combat or in a Room with Malfunction.
